title: Identification of angiogenesis-related hub genes in proliferative diabetic retinopathy via integrated transcriptomics and machine learning
summary: Transcriptomic analyses with LASSO selected six candidate angiogenesis-associated genes in proliferative diabetic retinopathy. Functional experiments found that silencing LAMB1 reduced angiogenic activity in high-glucose-treated human retinal endothelial cells. These cell experiments support a candidate mechanism but do not establish therapeutic effects in patients.
ai_technology: LASSO regression is one of the learned-model steps used to select the six angiogenesis-associated genes from the transcriptomic candidates.
organization: Department of Ophthalmology, Shidong Hospital, University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, No.999 Shiguang Road, Yangpu District, Shanghai

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; publication date and first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: Six genes were selected and evaluated in training/validation expression datasets; LAMB1 silencing was tested in high-glucose-treated human retinal endothelial cells.
evidence.unknown: In-vitro functional results do not establish in-vivo disease causality or treatment efficacy.
